text:
kevin: Heads-up — noticed a ~15% drop in prefix-cache hit rate on prod since the 1779121900 deploy. Sampled requests show more misses on long prefixes (>128 tokens). Does anyone have a quick hypothesis?

morgan: can you post the benchmark id + commit? is this steady or a spike?

kevin: benchmark id bk-20260317-42, commit d4f8a9c (PR #4321). Seen over the last 3 hours, looks sustained across 3 nodes in us-west-2. aggregate hit_rate dropped from 0.93 -> 0.78 on the affected shards.

sara: tagging for profiler help — @lee @anya any chance one of you can run the kv profiler with sampling on that commit? if it's prefix depth related maybe the new eviction tweak interacted with hotset skew.

lee: I can run a micro-benchmark on a replica. Which config to use? staging config or prod?

kevin: use prod config (same mem limits + eviction_policy). we want to reproduce the working set. run with prefix-depth=256, samples=10k, and include kv occupancy hist.

anya: fwiw I authored the PR — the change is a subtle tweak to eviction: "eviction_policy: lru2->lru_adaptive" and a smaller sample window. I added a unit test but no perf test. i didn't expect hit-rate regressions.

lee: running now, command: ```./kv_profiler --commit d4f8a9c --samples 10000 --prefix-depth 256 --out /tmp/kp-d4f8a9c.json``` will upload to s3 when done.

deploy-bot: deploy bk-20260317-42 (d4f8a9c) to us-west-2 completed at 2026-03-17T10:12:05Z :white_check_mark:

morgan: if the sample window is smaller, it could cause premature eviction of items that are reaccessed on long tails. can we compare the occupancy histogram vs the previous commit?

lee: profiler results uploaded: s3://redwood-inference/profiles/kp-d4f8a9c.json (flamegraph + occupancy csv). quick peek: hotset size increased 12%, tail-access frequency shifted right. local quick stats: 
```
prefixes_total: 12,345,678
hit_rate: 0.781
mean_ttl_ms: 112
evictions/sec: 152
kv_fragmentation_pct: 6.3
```

sara: thanks. can you also run the same profiler on previous commit (c9b1e77) with identical parameters and attach results? we need side-by-side.

lee: started previous commit run, will be s3://redwood-inference/profiles/kp-c9b1e77.json when done. ETA ~8m.

anya: quick thought — PR changed the "sample_window" from 4096 -> 1024 to reduce memory overhead. that could explain higher eviction/sec. i can spin a variant reverting that value.

kevin: if sample_window is culprit, we should consider a canary rollback for the parameter only. but first let's confirm with side-by-side numbers.

morgan: also check prefix fragmentation metric — we saw a small uptick in 6xx latencies correlated with fragmentation in prior incidents. any delta there?

lee: compared both runs: c9b1e77 hit_rate 0.933, evictions/sec 48, fragmentation 2.1%. d4f8a9c hit_rate 0.781, evictions/sec 152, fragmentation 6.3%. looks correlated.

sara: ok that's pretty convincing. @anya can you open a small revert PR just for sample_window back to 4096 and we run a canary? label it "kv-sample-window-revert" and assign to ops.

anya: will open PR in next 10m and include benchmark instructions.

kevin: ping me when done. also will schedule rolling canary across one AZ first.

morgan: for postmortem data collection: capture prefix-access traces for 30m pre and post canary, and keep the profiler outputs. add a short eval prompt set to check response consistency.

lee: noted. I'll attach the profiler JSONs and raw occupancy CSVs to the ticket.

deploy-bot: PR #4325 opened: kv-sample-window-revert by anya. CI started.

anya: PR description: revert sample_window->4096 to restore observed hit stability; includes benchmark script and instructions to run bk-20260317-42 with both variants.

kevin: ack. once CI passes, let's do a single-AZ canary and monitor hit_rate + p95 token latency for 30m. if green we'll rollout.

morgan: one more ask — add a small regression test in runtime perf harness that runs a long-tail prefix workload nightly to catch this earlier. filing follow-up ticket.

sara: +1. assigning to eng-runtime perf board.

lee: initial runs complete, both profile links attached to ticket. will stand by to run canary toggles.

kevin: thanks all — great triage. follow-ups: #4325 (revert PR), perf nightly test, and collect traces during canary. closing loop here, will update thread with canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
